curriculum: Groningen’s English-taught BSc Econometrics and Operations Research, ISAT 56833, has 180 EC. The 2026–27 scheme supplies one common set of twelve 5 EC courses in each of the first two years and a common third-year scheme. The four advertised profiles describe areas of study. They do not establish four separate 180 EC comparator curricula. The third year consists of an approved 30 EC minor or foreign minor, a 5 EC EOR elective, three required 5 EC courses and a 10 EC individual thesis. The elective must come from the EOR list or be individually approved. The foreign minor is approved and subject to course level, overlap and relevance rules. No specific elective, minor or profile is chosen for the general comparator.
progression: Year 1 starts with introductory calculus, OR modelling and data analytics, then programming, linear algebra and probability. Analysis follows those mathematics courses, with multivariate calculus, distributions and statistical modelling in block 2B. Year 2 places advanced linear algebra before convex optimisation, and probability and distributions before stochastic OR. OR Modelling precedes Discrete Operations Research. Linear Models precedes Introduction to Econometrics in 2A, which in turn precedes Dynamic Econometrics in 2B. Year 3 Numerical Methods expects programming and statistical inference. Games, Competition and Markets builds on second-year Game Theory. The normal thesis is in the second semester, with an alternative first-semester offering. Entry requires 120 EC, including all 60 EC of year one, and an approved 180 EC degree plan. Normal progression reaches this before the thesis. The thesis requires an individual scientific report with a mathematical model, methods and interpretation.
components: Choose one approved 30 EC minor or a semester abroad.
An individual modelling project and research report. The normal placement is the second semester of Year 3.
Choose a 5 EC course from the programme list or obtain approval for another course.

y1-statmod.title: Statistical Modelling for EOR
y1-statmod.prerequisites:
Familiarity with statistics and programming, as provided by participation in the first-year courses Probability Theory for EOR, Programming for EOR and Probability Distributions, is recommended.

Admittance to the BSc EOR (contact the programme coordinator for questions).

y2-macro.title: Macroeconomics for EOR
y2-macro.prerequisites:
Students must be comfortable with:
- Algebra.
- Calculus (mainly partial and total derivatives, and optimisation).
- First-order difference equations.
- Plotting equations as curves on figures and manipulating them (slopes and intercepts).
It is highly recommended that students brush up on these skills before the start of the course.

y2-linear.title: Math V: Advanced Linear Algebra
y2-linear.prerequisites: Familiarity with the basic principles in linear algebra (solving systems of equations, performing elementary matrix operations, computing determinants, and computing eigenvalues and eigenvectors). Thinking level of a student who successfully participated in the previous four math courses of the BSc EOR.

y2-convex.title: Math VI: Convexity and Optimization
y2-convex.prerequisites: The contents of Math I: Calculus, Math II: Linear Algebra, Math III: Analysis, Math IV: Multivariate Calculus, and Math V: Advanced Linear Algebra.

y2-stoch-or.title: Stochastic Operations Research
y2-stoch-or.prerequisites:
Participants should have an understanding of basic probability concepts such as taught in the courses Probability Theory for EOR and Probability Distributions. In particular:
* Probability density and distribution functions.
* Joint distribution and density, marginal distributions and densities.
* Conditional probability for (mixtures of) discrete and continuous random variables (Condition distribution functions, conditional density functions).
* Expectation, conditional expectation, conditional variance.
* Moment generating functions.

y2-discrete-or.title: Discrete Operations Research
y2-discrete-or.prerequisites: Full knowledge of the content of the course OR Modelling (EBP821B05).

y2-econometrics.title: Introduction to Econometrics
y2-econometrics.prerequisites: Students are expected to be familiar with the topics discussed in the course Linear Models in Statistics.

y2-dynamic.title: Dynamic Econometrics
y2-dynamic.prerequisites:
Notions of econometrics, statistics and mathematics considered in previous courses of the BSc EOR program, in particular the courses Probability Theory for EOR, Probability Distributions, Statistical Modelling for EOR, Statistical Inference, Linear Models in Statistics, and Introduction to Econometrics. Participants in the course need to know
(a) matrix algebra, determinants, convergence of deterministic sequences, difference equations,
(b) the topics considered in chapters 1.1-2.9 of the book by F. Hayashi,
(c) standard theory on estimation and hypothesis testing for models of independent and identically distributed random variables (including asymptotic results involving LLN, CLT, CMT and stochastic convergence modes).
In addition, the course requires familiarity with some software to perform statistical data analysis (in particular R).

y2-game.title: Game Theory
y2-game.prerequisites: Exchange students should have a very solid background in mathematics and probability theory at a level comparable to second-year students of the BSc EOR.

y3-numerical.title: Numerical Methods for EOR
y3-numerical.prerequisites: Programming at the level of Programming for EOR (EBP039A05) and statistics at the level of Statistical Inference (EBB075A05).

y3-thesis.title: Bachelor's Thesis EOR
y3-thesis.prerequisites:
BSc EOR students must have obtained at least 120 ECTS of the BSc programme (all 60 ECTS year 1 and at least 60 ECTS of years 2 and 3). The BSc programme (a complete 180 ECTS programme, including courses that haven't been passed yet) has to be approved.

Pre-MSc EORAS students must have passed Macroeconomics for EOR (EBB027B05), Math V: Advanced Linear Algebra (EBB157A05), and Statistical Inference (EBB075A05).

y3-games.title: Games, Competition and Markets
y3-games.prerequisites: Exchange students should have solid knowledge of game theory, as taught in the second-year course Game Theory of the BSc EOR.

schemeEvidence.thirdYearRules:
The minor EOR is recommended for students who wish to register for the MSc Econometrics, Operations Research & Actuarial Studies or a similar programme.
The minors Business and Taxation and Education Mathematics are taught in Dutch.
The courses of the study abroad programme (foreign minor) can contain a maximum of 15 EC that do not contribute to the learning outcomes of the BSc EOR, including no more than one language course in the language of the foreign university (maximum 6 EC). The courses of the study abroad programme must be postpropaedeutic and not overlap with the other courses of the BSc EOR programme followed by the student. The courses of the study abroad programme should be approved by the programme coordinator of the BSc EOR. A student can submit a substitution request to the programme coordinator (via eor@rug.nl) with a proposal consisting of courses from the faculty minor EOR or from the elective courses EOR to replace the failed course(s). A substitution request can only be submitted if a student obtains at least 20 out of the 30 EC from the approved foreign minor. A student who has obtained less than 20 EC of the approved foreign minor has to complete an entirely different minor.
Students who already passed Introduction to Mathematical Economics (EBB872A05) need to take Game Theory (EBB872A05), listed under year 2 instead of Games, Competition and Markets (EBB148A05).
Students who do not choose the minor EOR can choose a course of this minor as elective BSc EOR.
Students who want to choose an elective that is not on the list have to contact the coordinator of the BSc EOR for approval.
It is not allowed to choose the university minor Entrepreneurship.
It is not allowed to combine parts of different minors.
Bachelor’s Thesis EOR (EBB925A10) can also be taken in semester 1.
